t: Long, long ago, in the city of Susa, there lived a very powerful king. His name was King Xerxes.
m: Narrator | storyteller opening; warm, unhurried, a little mysterious; small pause before the name | at most 9.0 s
d: Picture: bedtime, a big picture book open, the child leaning on you. (Esther 1:1-2)

t: The king chose a beautiful, kind young woman to be his queen. Her name was Esther.
m: Narrator | tender, smiling; slow down on her name | at most 7.4 s
d: Picture: you are introducing someone you love. (Esther 2:7, 2:17)

t: Make way for the great Lord Haman!
m: Herald (off-stage) | off-stage court herald: loud and long, ceremonial, a little pompous | at most 6.0 s
d: Picture: at the doors of a great hall, announcing someone to a crowded room. (Esther 3:1)

t: Hail, Lord Haman!
m: Crowd (off-stage) | many people at once, off-stage, bowing; a little reluctant | at most 3.9 s
d: Picture: a crowd bowing and calling out together. (Esther 3:2)

t: Ho ho! Did you see that? Everyone bows when I walk by! I'm the greatest man in the whole kingdom! Ha ha ha ha!
m: Haman | hugely pleased with himself, nose in the air, savouring every word; a real belly laugh at the end that goes on a bit too long | at most 10.0 s
d: Picture: you just won first prize and stand on the stage, hands on hips, laughing. (Esther 3:1-2)

t: But one man would not bow. Mordecai said, "I bow only to God."
m: Narrator | calm, a little amused; a small pause before Mordecai's words | at most 6.9 s
d: Picture: telling about someone with real backbone, a smile at the corner of your mouth. (Esther 3:2-4)

t: What?! He won't bow to ME?! Grrr! Hmph! Hmph! Hmph!
m: Haman | explodes: shrill, spluttering fury, a tantrum; three stamping 'hmph's, each louder; comic, not scary | at most 6.0 s
d: Picture: someone grabbed your toy and you stamp your feet in a rage. (Esther 3:5)

t: O king... there are some people who don't keep your laws. Why not... let me get rid of them?
m: Haman | sly half-whisper, slow, oily, sugary-sweet to the king; two sneaky pauses | at most 11.1 s
d: Picture: whispering in someone's ear, eyes darting left and right. (Esther 3:8-9)

t: Hmm... very well. Take my ring. Do as you see fit.
m: King Xerxes | deep, careless, a little bored; a thinking 'hmm' first | at most 6.3 s
d: Picture: slumped in a big chair, handing something over without looking. (Esther 3:10-11)

t: Heh heh heh... Now nobody can stop me!
m: Haman | turns to the audience, rubbing his hands; a wicked little giggle, then gleeful | at most 3.0 s
d: Picture: you got the cookie jar and giggle to yourself. (Esther 3:10-11)

t: Esther, you must ask the king to save us! Maybe this is why you became queen, for a time just like this!
m: Mordecai (off-stage) | older man, urgent but loving, from a distance; slower on the last sentence | at most 7.1 s
d: Picture: outside a door, speaking through it to someone you love. (Esther 4:8, 4:14)

t: But... anyone who goes to the king without being called could die...
m: Esther | scared, quiet, hesitant; breath before 'but' | at most 7.3 s
d: Picture: you want to help, but you are shaking inside. (Esther 4:11)

t: All right. Please pray for me. I will go to the king, even if it's dangerous!
m: Esther | a deep breath, then steady and brave; rising resolve, strongest on the last words | at most 6.3 s
d: Picture: you wipe your tears, stand up and decide. (Esther 4:16)

t: Step by step, Esther climbed the palace stairs... What would the king do?
m: Narrator | hushed, suspenseful, slow; let the question hang | at most 8.7 s
d: Picture: the scariest part of the story; the child holds their breath. (Esther 5:1)

t: Queen Esther! You've come. What is it you want? Even half my kingdom, it's yours!
m: King Xerxes | surprised, then warm and generous; a smile in the voice | at most 7.0 s
d: Picture: someone you love turns up by surprise and you are glad. (Esther 5:2-3)

t: My king, will you come to my banquet? And bring Haman too.
m: Esther | polite, sweet, a little clever; light | at most 3.9 s
d: Picture: inviting someone to dinner with a smile, a plan in mind. (Esther 5:4)

t: The queen's banquet! Only the king... and ME! Ha! Aren't I wonderful!
m: Haman | giddy, bouncing with glee, almost singing; a pause before 'and me', then a delighted laugh | at most 7.8 s
d: Picture: you just got the party invitation you wanted most. (Esther 5:9-12)

t: Haman, there is a man I want to honour. What should I do for him?
m: King Xerxes | thoughtful, kind, slow; a real question | at most 5.0 s
d: Picture: wondering how to surprise a good friend. (Esther 6:6)

t: Heh heh... who could that be, but me?
m: Haman | a stage whisper to the audience behind his hand; smug, delighted | at most 3.2 s
d: Picture: telling the audience a secret behind your hand: it's me, of course! (Esther 6:6)

t: Dress him in the royal robe! Sit him on the king's own horse! And have someone shout: "This is the man the king honours!"
m: Haman | grand, dreamy, carried away, bigger and bigger; the last phrase shouted proudly like a herald | at most 9.4 s
d: Picture: daydreaming that you ride a great horse through the streets in a royal robe. (Esther 6:7-9)

t: Good idea! Now go and do all of that for Mordecai!
m: King Xerxes | pleased, warm, brisk; a smile; the name clear and simple | at most 4.3 s
d: Picture: you love the idea and decide on the spot. (Esther 6:10)

t: Mor... Mor... MORDECAI?!
m: Haman | can't believe it: choking, stammering, then a strangled squeak on the name | at most 3.5 s
d: Picture: you were sure the prize was yours, and it goes to the person you like least. (Esther 6:10-11)

t: So Haman had to lead Mordecai through the city on the king's horse, shouting all the way...
m: Narrator | trying not to laugh; storyteller relishing the twist | at most 7.0 s
d: Picture: telling a funny ending and nearly laughing yourself. (Esther 6:11)

t: This... is the man the king honours... hmph!
m: Haman | through gritted teeth, sulky, flat and grudging; a dying-off 'hmph' | at most 4.7 s
d: Picture: you are made to praise, out loud, the person you like least. (Esther 6:11)

t: My king... someone wants to destroy me, and all my people!
m: Esther | trembling but brave; voice catches on 'my people' | at most 4.5 s
d: Picture: you find the courage to say something that hurts. (Esther 7:3-4)

t: What?! Who is he? Who would dare?
m: King Xerxes | shocked and angry, loud but not shouting; short sharp phrases | at most 3.0 s
d: Picture: you hear someone has been hurting the person you love most. (Esther 7:5)

t: It's him! This wicked man, Haman!
m: Esther | clear and firm, a beat of courage before 'Haman' | at most 3.1 s
d: Picture: you point straight at the one who did wrong. (Esther 7:6)

t: No, no, no! My queen, save me! Oh king, have mercy!
m: Haman | blubbering, squeaky panic, fast and breathless, close to tears; comic | at most 7.2 s
d: Picture: caught red-handed, your knees turn to jelly. (Esther 7:7-8)

t: Guards! Take him away!
m: King Xerxes | a royal command: loud, deep and final; not a scream | at most 2.1 s
d: Picture: you slap the arm of your chair and command the guards. (Esther 7:8-9)

t: Nooo! Let me go! I'm a very important man! I'm... waaaah!
m: Haman | wailing and kicking as he is dragged off; a long howling 'no', then outraged, then a big wail that fades away into the distance | at most 8.4 s
d: Picture: being dragged off to the bath, howling all the way. (Esther 7:8)

t: The king had Haman taken away. God's people were saved! Everyone sang and danced for joy!
m: Narrator | relief, then bright joy; speed up a little on the happy part | at most 7.7 s
d: Picture: the danger is over; you and the child clap together. (Esther 7:10, 8:16-17)

t: Esther was scared, but she chose to be brave and to trust God. You can too!
m: Narrator | warm moral, speaking right to the child; smile on 'You can too' | at most 8.2 s
d: Picture: you look the child in the eyes and stroke their hair. (Esther 4:14-16)
